source: User report (2026-08-12): Agent Teams sessions end their turn with work still open — 'All 17 items are assigned and no lane is idle. It's the turn boundary: every time my turn is about to end, I fill it with a summary. Writing a summary forces me to decide what's done enough to describe, and that decision is me drawing the boundary again.' The user has exhausted the instruction tier ('make a list of my outstanding asks' / 'you cannot consider anything complete until you have finished all my asks') and asks whether ralph loops would lock the agent in, and what else can be done. Refined brief: .architect-team/refined-prompts/agent-teams-completion-lock-20260812T051212Z.md (grade 88.9/B, exit-reason user-confirmed).

baseline.note: MEASURED at Phase 0 on branch architect-team/turn-boundary-completion-lock before any edit; the number is from that run, not carried from the CHANGELOG. Gate is zero NEW failures vs the measured baseline. Two byte-count tests (test_installer_guidance_blocks, test_skill_references) are KNOWN pre-existing Windows line-ending failures since the v3.42.x macOS merges — if present in the baseline they stay in the allowed set and are not this run's regressions. check_separation unaffected (hooks tier, no new services module) — stays 26.

user_decisions: Blast radius: EVERY session, always (not CT6-run-gated) — the arm fires with no CT6 run present
Escape hatch: UNBOUNDED — never allow stop; only a named kill-switch releases it (the agent can never decide to stop, the user always can)
Source of truth: BOTH the harness task list AND an ask-ledger
ralph-loop: verified disk-read exit SUPERSEDES it at the top level; ralph stays in the convergence sub-loops
Turn output: ENFORCE the one-line-of-state rule (not instruction-tier only)
Teammates: block on OWNED items only (not a wholesale standdown)
Ledger: AUTO-DERIVED from transcript prompts (harness-written), not model-registered

entries.spec_requirement_id: turn-boundary-completion-lock/A session cannot end its turn while registered work is open
acceptance_criteria: A plain session with >=1 task at pending|in_progress in ~/.claude/tasks/session-<8>/ and NO .architect-team/ run state -> the Stop hook BLOCKS (red-first; this is the reported bug)
Zero open tasks + empty/absent ledger -> exit 0, no false positives in ordinary sessions (test)

The lock is evaluated ABOVE the non-engaged early return (:1757-1763) AND above the budget return (:1774-1783) AND above the escalation-marker return (:1706) — pinned by the engaged 10-stop test and the escalation-marker test, not by reading the source
The pre-existing arms are untouched: _is_real_run still gates audit(), CT6_MAX_NO_PROGRESS_STOPS still governs them, existing tests/test_pipeline_completion_audit*.py stay green

entries.spec_requirement_id: turn-boundary-completion-lock/Blocking is unbounded and released only by a named kill-switch
acceptance_criteria: In an ENGAGED session, 10 consecutive no-progress stop attempts with open work still BLOCK every time — no budget escape (test must exercise the engaged path; a non-engaged-only test could pass while the engaged case stayed broken)
Four named kill-switches implemented and asserted by name: CT6_COMPLETION_LOCK_DISABLED (master) + CT6_TASK_LIST_GATE_DISABLED + CT6_ASK_LEDGER_GATE_DISABLED + CT6_TURN_OUTPUT_GATE_DISABLED
Per-source independence: setting the ledger switch leaves the task-list source enforcing (test)

entries.spec_requirement_id: turn-boundary-completion-lock/The ask-ledger is derived from the transcript and accumulates durably
acceptance_criteria: An unresolved ledger entry blocks the stop even when the harness task list is EMPTY (test)

TAIL-CAP TEST: a stored entry whose originating turn is NOT in the available transcript slice still counts as open and still blocks — re-derivation is purely additive and never removes or reopens a stored entry (the test that matters most; without it the ledger silently under-reports on long sessions)
Entries derive from harness-written transcript prompts, NOT a model-initiated registration call; an ambiguous entry stays OPEN (conservative resolution; over-blocking fails safe)
Ledger writes use the atomic tmp-then-replace pattern (run_continuity.py:282), stored at .architect-team/ask-ledger.json

entries.spec_requirement_id: turn-boundary-completion-lock/A pipeline teammate is held only for work it owns
acceptance_criteria: A teammate session with open tasks NONE of which it owns -> ALLOWED to stop (test)
A teammate session with >=1 open task whose owner matches it -> BLOCKED, message names that task (test)
An unidentifiable teammate falls back to the existing standdown — never wedged (test); reuses run_continuity.is_teammate_transcript (:724) + TEAMMATE_TOKEN (:88-94), no parallel detector

entries.spec_requirement_id: turn-boundary-completion-lock/While work is open the turn output is one line of state, not a narrative
acceptance_criteria: TRIPS: open work + a last assistant text block that is >=3 non-empty lines OR carries a heading / bullet or numbered item / **Label:** block / table row -> re-blocks, message states the rule (test each marker kind)
DOES NOT TRIP: a one-line state output, and a two-line marker-free terse status update (test BOTH — a rule that never fires is decoration; a rule that fires on a terse update gets disabled)
classify_turn_output is a pure function over a string with no I/O (exhaustively unit-testable); reads the last assistant text block via the reused run_continuity transcript reader

entries.spec_requirement_id: turn-boundary-completion-lock/An own-code crash fails open but an unreadable source blocks
acceptance_criteria: A malformed/unreadable task JSON -> BLOCKS and the message NAMES that source (test) — a blanket fail-open here would reproduce the reported bug via one bad file
A crash injected into the lock's own code -> exit 0 with a stderr note (test), matching main()'s wrapper at :1791-1793
Source-read failures are carried as DATA (an unreadable[] partition), never as exceptions, so only unexpected control-flow errors reach the fail-open wrapper
The .lock / .highwatermark sidecars are skipped BY NAME, never via a silent parse failure (test)
Every harness-task reader accepts an injected root (explicit arg > env override > real home) so the suite points at tmp_path; NO test writes to the user's real ~/.claude/tasks store (pinned)
Paired review: independent task-reviewer + adversarial-reviewer, producer != checker, evidence-schema-v7, validate_evidence 0 gaps; attack list per tasks 6.1

Full suite zero NEW failures vs the MEASURED baseline, both encodings; check_separation green and unchanged (26); verify-check-can-fail verdict for every new test file; a captured demo (open tasks -> blocked; closed -> allowed; each kill-switch -> no-op)

The ralph-loop non-adoption rationale is WRITTEN DOWN so a later run does not re-adopt it; cites ONLY the verified twelve ralph-loop-using skills (there is no exploration-pipeline skill — a phantom citation fails tests/test_instruction_compliance.py)

The FOUR kill-switches are documented in the README — a gate this broad must be releasable by a user who has never read the source
